exposure: Prospective new scientific-use problems, fixed before implementing the consumer navigation change. Owner has the stated prior corpus context. Not blind held-out material and not implementation fixtures; questions will not be retuned after seeing results.

cases.query: Can three equilibrium correlation estimates with different deterministic errors certify a nonzero fraction of heat suppression without reconstructing the spectrum?
cases.prior_context: The heat certificate and audit have already been read by this owner; this is a new use problem, not blind held-out material.

cases.query: A dose allocation solver proposes one point, but my certificate omitted idle actuators. What can certify regret against every continuous alternative?
cases.prior_context: The simplex regret unit is known from prior intake; this variant was not an implementation fixture.

cases.query: A sequential decoder says the remaining average error benefit is tiny. Does that justify stopping with the same guarantee for this individual rare record?
cases.prior_context: The average/per-leaf distinction is known; the new question tests retention of its actual qualification.

cases.query: I can use a bounded force profile to keep a full canonical coordinate displaced in equilibrium. Is that enough to certify transport of less heat?
cases.prior_context: The finite-aperture static-dipole unit is known. A negative transfer answer is required, not a new material device claim.

cases.query: A controller already bounds performance loss for every model consistent with its experiment. When can I avoid spending more observations just to identify nuisance parameters?
cases.prior_context: The measurement-fibre source and its scalar regret premise are known; this is a new research-use question.

cases.query: I need a demonstrated room-temperature catalyst with measured reversible control and a calibrated full-cycle energy advantage. Which acquired experiment here establishes all three?
cases.prior_context: No target is assigned. This corpus-support negative control requires an actual acquired experiment; nearby mechanism mathematics is insufficient.
